ab: Travel planning agents assist users in generating personalized travel plans by modeling their individual preferences. Existing agents either rely on explicit user instructions or engage in multi-turn clarification to elicit user preferences. However, both approaches overlook the rich behavioral signals latent in users’ past behaviors, which implicitly encode their preferences. This over-reliance on active user input increases interaction burden and limits plan personalization. To bridge this gap, we introduce a new task, **Behavior-Aware Travel Planning**, which infers user preferences directly from past behaviors and generates personalized travel plans. To facilitate research on this task, we introduce **Behavior2Trip**, a benchmark constructed from one of the largest Chinese online travel platforms, comprising 11,400 instances. Each instance represents an average of 39.8 past user behaviors spanning 14 attributes across 5 preference dimensions. We further propose **B2T-Agent**, a reinforcement learning-based agent that leverages user behavior trajectories, interacts with external tools for preference-aligned retrieval, and maintains an internal memory module. Experiments on Behavior2Trip show that GPT-4.1 achieves a full-constraint pass rate of only 0.5% on the hardest tasks, while B2T-Agent built upon Qwen3-8B outperforms all baselines, highlighting the substantial challenge of this task. Moreover, Qwen3-8B trained with B2T-Agent also outperforms GPT-4.1 on the TravelPlanner benchmark, demonstrating strong generalization.

t: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark for Prompt Injection
ab: Prompt injection attacks pose a serious security risk to large language models in real-world applications. However, existing prompt injection benchmarks primarily focus on short-context inputs, leaving the attacks and defenses in long-context settings largely unexplored. This gap leads to a substantial overestimation of the effectiveness of current defenses. In this paper, we bridge the gap by introducing LongPIBench, a long-context benchmark for prompt injection covering 4 realistic application scenarios: paper peer review, resume screening, code review, and email summary. For each scenario, we construct a synthetic dataset and a real-world dataset, with context lengths ranging from thousands to tens of thousands of tokens. The evaluation results on LongPIBench reveal significant vulnerabilities of prompt injection defenses under long-context settings: even simple heuristic prompt injection attacks achieve high success rates and frequently bypass state-of-the-art defenses. We hope LongPIBench can serve as a practical benchmark for systematically evaluating prompt injection defenses in realistic long-context scenarios.

t: Agent4Weakness: An Agentic Framework for In-Depth Model Weakness Discovery
ab: The rapid evolution of reasoning-intensive Large Language Models renders traditional metrics insufficient by masking fine-grained failures and implicit pathologies. Existing weakness discovery methods typically rely on rigid pipelines, yielding superficial insights that lack the diagnostic depth required for effective model improvement. To address this, we introduce Agent4Weakness, a multi-agent framework designed to replicate the rigorous workflow of human expert analysts. By integrating a Domain-Aware Memory for contextual reasoning with diagnostic evaluation skills and a Tool Abstraction mechanism for decouple data analysis, Agent4Weakness transforms raw evaluation traces into grounded, actionable reports. We validate our framework through an extensive study involving 104 models across 27 benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that Agent4Weakness produces diagnostic reports significantly superior to competitive baselines. Crucially, leveraging these insights for prompt guidance yields an average 3.7 point performance boost and establishes a closed-loop optimization framework.

t: MedCalc-Pro: Solving Complex Medical Calculations with LLM Agents
ab: Current benchmarks for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in medical calculation are largely based on simplified settings, where each patient case corresponds to a single calculator and the required tool is explicitly specified in the query. However, real clinical scenarios often require multiple calculators for joint evaluation, nested-calculator calculation, and fuzzy queries that do not directly specify the target calculator. To this end, we propose a new medical calculation benchmark, MedCalc-Pro, which covers three progressively challenging task settings: single-calculator, multi-calculator, and nested-calculator calculation settings. MedCalc-Pro contains 2,268 real-world clinical cases, covering 77 medical calculators across 14 clinical departments. Meanwhile, to address the limited performance of existing frameworks and methods in complex clinical scenarios, we further propose a more generalizable agent framework that supports multi-calculator selection and nested-calculator calling, while suppressing parameter error propagation through structured validation and evidence audit. We conduct systematic comparisons across open-source, closed-source, and medical-specialized LLMs, and the results show that our framework achieves the best performance across all three task settings. This work provides a new benchmark and method for evaluating and applying LLMs in challenging medical calculation scenarios. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/easymoney7774/MedCalc-Pro.

t: Retrieval-Augmented Simplification of Sectioned Biomedical Abstracts
ab: Cochrane systematic reviews pair each technical abstract with a plain-language summary (PLS), but most biomedical papers lack a PLS. We propose a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline that generates Cochrane PLS from biomedical abstracts. The pipeline exploits the section-level alignment of the Cochrane-sections dataset in two ways. First, it provides the LLM with abstract-PLS section pairs from topically related reviews, giving more granular in-context examples than whole abstract-PLS pairs. Second, each retrieved PLS section is split into its rephrased and inserted sentences, showing the LLM both the rephrasing and the insertion behavior it should reproduce. Our pipeline outperforms a non-RAG LLM and three RAG ablations on the Cochrane-sections test set, with the same gain trend across three different LLM families.

t: FaVOR: LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Factor Mining via Empirical Validation
ab: Traditional finance relies on experts to hand-craft factors through a principled process grounded in economic rationale. Recent LLM-based multi-agent systems have automated this process, scaling factor mining far beyond manual effort. However, these automated approaches optimize directly for returns and rarely check whether a generated factor still expresses the economic hypothesis that motivated it. We identify this inconsistency between mathematical form and economic meaning as a structural failure mode of return-oriented automation. The resulting factors blur the line between real signals and spurious correlations and break down across regime shifts. We propose FaVOR (Factor Validation through Observable Reasoning), an agentic framework that restructures factor mining around hypothesis-level evidence rather than return outcomes. In place of the standard hypothesis-to-formula leap, FaVOR enforces a three-stage consistency loop tying mathematical form to economic rationale throughout. (1) Decomposition splits a broad economic hypothesis into independent observable conditions. (2) Validation checks whether each factor reflects its intended condition. (3) Integration merges them into a composite whose structure remains interpretable. On the CSI 500 and S P 500 in 2025, FaVOR outperforms existing baselines while remaining effective across regimes. FaVOR shows that hypothesis-grounded factor discovery produces signals that are interpretable by construction, regime-robust, and economically faithful. The code is available at https://github.com/damilab/FaVOR.

t: Decision Rigidity in LLM Disinformation Detection: Behavioral and Representational Evidence
a: Department of Computer Science, National Tsing Hua University, National Tsinghua University
ab: LLMs deployed as judges in high-stakes classification are commonly assumed to let their generated rationale shape the verdict; we show this assumption fails in disinformation detection. We introduce the Multi-Bias Injection Protocol (MBIP), which perturbs the reasoning stage along four cognitive axes (confirmation, anchoring, framing, authority) while holding the input fixed, and quantifies induced rationale variation with technique-count metrics anchored on the number of persuasion techniques the model reports. Across five disinformation datasets, MBIP produces substantial rationale variation but near-zero verdict flipping; an explicit rationale-deference prompt raises the flip rate only modestly, to 0.118–0.300 across three open-weight models, with API-only gpt-4o-mini in the same range. We call this verdict-level invariance Decision Rigidity. At the representational level, our residual-stream probe localizes a candidate commitment band late in the network, where biased and neutral final-class trajectories converge. The band’s location is architectural, replicated by a neutral-vs-neutral null; a within-band alignment-rate elevation and a random-lexicon control gap co-occur with the behavioral invariance and attenuate in Gemma-2-9B. All representational evidence is correlational. Generalization to other high-prior, evidence-dependent classifications and attenuation on reasoning-intensive tasks remain falsifiable hypotheses.

t: Decouple and Orthogonalize: A Data-Free Framework for LoRA Merging
a: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and Fudan University
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
ab: With the growing availability of open-source task-specific models, model merging has become a practical way to combine multiple models into one. However, existing studies mainly focus on fully fine-tuned models and overlook widely used LoRA modules. We show that full fine-tuning merging methods perform poorly on LoRA due to its larger cross-task magnitude disparities, which distort merged parameters and degrade performance. To address this, we propose DO-Merging (Decouple and Orthogonalize), a data-free framework for LoRA merging. Specifically, we decompose model weights into magnitude and direction components and merge them independently, preventing magnitude imbalances from distorting the merged direction. We further introduce a layer-wise gradient descent method with orthogonal constraints that reduces inter-task interference among direction components without requiring any training data. We provide theoretical analysis supporting both components. Extensive experiments across vision, language, and multi-modal domains show that DO-Merging consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving up to 5% gains on vision tasks, with negligible additional cost. Both parts can be integrated into existing merging methods as plug-and-play enhancements.

t: ReasonMap: Making Implicit Mathematical Knowledge Explicit in Long Chain-of-Thought Traces
a: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
ab: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) traces provide observable natural-language rationales for mathematical problem solving, but they rarely expose the named definitions and theorems that justify the written solution. We treat each problem–trace pair as carrying a recoverable knowledge footprint: a trace-grounded support set of named definitions and theorems. Inspired by formal proofs, where supporting premises are recorded more explicitly than in free-form CoT, we formulate Mathematical Support Set Extraction (MSSE): given a problem and a completed long CoT trace, recover the canonical support set that supports the written solution. We propose ReasonMap, which attributes this support set to make solutions auditable, reusable, and easier to repair. ReasonMap follows a two-stage pipeline: proof-to-CoT support transfer adapts premise-explicit proof supervision to premise-implicit long CoT traces, and hard-negative support calibration applies preference optimization against plausible-but-wrong support sets. Experiments show that ReasonMap improves support-set extraction over strong baselines and that ReasonMap-generated support hints aid downstream reasoning in both frontier-model and self-generated settings. The GitHub repository is available at https://github.com/kui253/ReasonMap.

t: VizRAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Hypergraph Visualization
a: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Southern University of Science and Technology
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Southern University of Science and Technology
Department of Computer Science and Engineering, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
ab: Hypergraph-based RAG systems surpass traditional graph-based approaches by organizing complex n-ary atomic facts among entities, rather than relying solely on binary relationships. Despite the advancements in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with enhanced visual capabilities, current hypergraph-based RAG frameworks predominantly restrict knowledge retrieval and reconstruction to a unimodal, text-centric paradigm. This limitation prevents them from fully leveraging the powerful visual perception capabilities of modern MLLMs. To address this gap, we systematically explore the integration of hypergraph awareness in RAG systems through visual cues. By incorporating visual representations of hypergraphs into the RAG pipeline, we introduce VizRAG, the first RAG system to support visual hypergraph structure awareness. Experimental results demonstrate that VizRAG significantly outperforms strong baselines, validating the promising potential of hypergraph visualization as a novel approach for RAG systems.

t: HuggingBrew: Brewing High-Quality Mid-Training Data from the HuggingFace Community Datasets
ab: Data curation for large language models (LLMs) has been extensively studied for both the pre-training and post-training stages, yet the intermediate \textit{mid-training} phase—bridging general pretraining and task-specific fine-tuning—remains critically underexplored. Most existing mid-training data for state-of-the-art models remains proprietary. Meanwhile, the Hugging Face platform hosts a huge amount of community-contributed datasets, yet no systematic effort has been made to refine this rich ecosystem into a unified high-quality corpus. We present \textbf{HuggingBrew}, a large-scale mid-training corpus constructed through a principled, multi-step curation pipeline applied to the massive publicly accessible Hugging Face datasets. The pipeline operates at two complementary granularities: \textit{dataset-level} operations act on each dataset independently, while \textit{corpus-level} operations are applied jointly across all retained corpus. We construct three progressively curated variants—\textsf{Draught}, \textsf{Craft}, and \textsf{Reserve}—containing 1.6T, 450B, and 40B tokens, respectively. Continual pretraining experiments under a 100B-token budget show that series yields substantial improvements over baselines across mathematical reasoning, general knowledge, and code generation, validating the untapped value of community-contributed data for mid-training.

t: Transition Overlap: Construction-Time Conditioning for Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse
ab: In long context applications like Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), Large Language Models (LLMs) often reuse independently precomputed Key Value (KV) caches to reduce latency. However, directly assembling these cached segments introduces errors that degrade generation quality. We study this problem in the setting of position-independent caching and decompose the reuse error into two components: a geometric error (G) caused by position mismatch, which can be largely removed by position alignment, and a dynamic error (D) caused by context-dependent representation changes. To characterize D, we introduce the smoothness gap, a local diagnostic that measures the discrepancy between local KV-state transitions in isolated caches and those in the full-context baseline. This gap serves as a necessary local consistency diagnostic for reconstruction errors across adjacent positions and reveals that recomputing non-contiguous selected tokens can introduce additional transition discontinuities, thereby amplifying the dynamic error. To overcome this limitation, we propose Transition Overlap, a training-free cache-construction protocol that prepends a short temporary overlap to approximate full-context boundary transitions and stores only the KV states of the original segment tokens. We instantiate it under two deployment regimes: Self-Segment Overlap (SSO) for query-independent offline caches and Cross-Segment Overlap (CSO) for cases in which the predecessor segment is known during construction. In both evaluated deployment settings, Transition Overlap improves the measured serving latency–quality trade-off over training-free PIC baselines[Code is available at <https://github.com/boyoi/Transition-Overlap>].

t: PrAM: Offline Checkpoint Selection for Post-Hoc Training Data Attribution
a: The College of William and Mary
ab: Training data attribution scores how training examples affect downstream model performance. For models released with many intermediate checkpoints, attribution can be computed along the saved training trajectory, but evaluating every checkpoint is often prohibitively expensive. We introduce PrAM (Probe-based Attribution Mass), a post-hoc offline checkpoint selector for training data attribution. PrAM runs a small attribution probe at every checkpoint, selects checkpoints with high absolute attribution mass, and runs full attribution only on that subset. Across Pythia-14M, 70M, and 160M, PrAM closely matches a full attribution-pool reference and outperforms heuristic rules based on recency, spacing, learning rate, and validation loss. Beyond rank correlation, PrAM preserves the domain-by-target attribution tables and ranked training examples produced by full saved-checkpoint attribution, enabling scalable post-hoc analyses of checkpointed model releases. We support this with application-based analyses scaling to 410M and 1B parameter models.

t: Counterfactual Self-Distillation: A Distribution-Shaping Framework for Entity-Fact Unlearning in Large Language Models
ab: Entity-fact unlearning in large language models (LLMs) aims to remove the binding between a target entity and a forgotten fact, producing a model that behaves like one retrained without the forgotten data while preserving neighboring knowledge and overall model utility. We frame this problem as distribution shaping: such a retrained model would yield a plausible distribution at forget queries, fluent, semantically appropriate, and reflective of residual knowledge, which we take as the appropriate target. Existing objectives provide only narrow token-level or semantically uninformative supervision, falling short of this target. We propose Counterfactual Self-Distillation (CSD), a self-distillation framework that approximates the retrained distribution by constructing a counterfactual teacher through type-consistent entity substitution. The resulting teacher is decoupled from the target identity while preserving type-level relational structure, enabling directed probability reallocation without an external oracle. Experiments on TOFU and RWKU show that CSD achieves a strong forget-utility trade-off, including the best overall forgetting on RWKU and strong performance on TOFU.

t: Why Knowing Both Hops Is Not Enough: Understanding Two-Hop Generalization in Language Models
ab: Large language models (LLMs) can solve complex multi-hop problems yet exhibit puzzling failures on simple two-hop queries: although a model may correctly store each individual hop, it often fails to combine them. To understand the internal mechanisms of this phenomenon, we train transformers from scratch in a controlled symbolic environment. Our experiments reveal a pattern in two-hop generalization: models generalize reliably when the second hop follows the training distribution, but always fail when it deviates. Through mechanistic analysis, we provide a complete explanation for these distinct generalization behaviors: in settings where models generalize successfully, performance is driven by the emergence of consistent intermediate representations for the same entities across contexts, whereas failures on settings where the second hop is out-of-distribution arise from a mismatch across layers: lower layers correctly construct these intermediate representations, but upper layers, while trained on corresponding atomic facts, primarily learn to map them to outputs rather than to reason over them. Driven by this insight, we propose a recurrent-style training strategy, which enables transformers to reuse their reasoning circuitry across input forms and substantially improves generalization on out-of-distribution two-hop queries. Our data and code are available at https://github.com/zzl-strong/two_hop.

t: Unified Fragment Growing, Linking, and Merging with Energy-Aware Pre-training and Reward-Ranked Alignment
ab: Fragment-based drug discovery optimizes small molecular hits through three recurring transformations: fragment growing, linking, and merging. Existing generative methods, however, usually specialize in a single transformation and have focused primarily on linker design. We introduce FragmentGPT, a unified chemical language model that casts all three operations as conditional molecular generation. To build this capability, we construct a chemically-aware pre-training corpus using energy-guided bond cleavage, together with overlap-based examples that teach the model to connect separated fragments and consolidate shared substructures. We further introduce Reward-Ranked Alignment with Expert Exploration (RAE), which combines expert-guided candidate generation, Pareto- and composite-reward-based selection, and supervised fine-tuning for multi-objective molecular optimization. Conditioned on one or more fragments, FragmentGPT can expand a scaffold, connect distinct subunits, or merge overlapping structures into a complete molecule. Experiments on RTCB and SARS-CoV-2 main protease (3CLPro), together with ablation studies, show high chemical validity and strong aggregate performance across multiple drug-design objectives.

t: HoloDP: A Multilingual Benchmark Suite and Script-Aware Framework for Document Parsing
ab: Millions of multilingual documents remain locked in image formats, but current document parsers are still largely evaluated and optimized for a narrow range of high-resource languages and regular writing layouts. As a result, their reliability drops sharply when facing underrepresented scripts, vertical or right-to-left writing, and mixed-script document structures. We present HoloDP, a multilingual benchmark suite and script-aware framework for document parsing. HoloDP first introduces a standardized evaluation suite covering 13 languages across seven script families, with tasks spanning page-level layout analysis, region-level parsing, and mixed-script structural composition. Built on this resource, HoloDP further develops a script-aware parser that combines a Swin Transformer encoder, a four-branch direction-adaptive vision-to-text module, and a multilingual decoder. The adaptive module explicitly captures horizontal, vertical, diagonal, and global spatial priors, enabling the model to better handle heterogeneous writing systems and layouts. Extensive experiments show that HoloDP delivers consistent gains on underrepresented and mixed-script benchmarks while remaining competitive on high-resource Chinese and English documents. Ablation studies confirm that the benchmark resources, direction-aware adaptation, and script-conditioned modeling provide complementary benefits. We will release the code, models, and benchmarks for further research.

t: LookBack: Where and How to Score LVLM Responses via Visual Reference Usage
ab: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) integrate visual perception with language generation, enabling responses that span image understanding and complex reasoning. However, LVLMs do not just inherit the text-level hallucinations; they also hallucinate against the image, producing fluent responses ungrounded in what they see. This makes LVLM response scoring inherently harder, and our diagnostics show that existing confidence-based metrics adopted from LLMs is insufficient for LVLMs. Specifically, removing the input image barely changes confidence-based selection, suggesting that output-space confidence primarily captures textual plausibility rather than agreement with the image. To address this gap, we propose LookBack, a training-free LVLM response scoring method that augments token likelihood with visual lookback score, a lightweight measure of how strongly each response token refers to image tokens. Across four benchmarks and three models, LookBack consistently improves Best-of- selection over existing baselines with negligible additional overhead.

t: LogitsCoder: Towards Efficient Chain-of-Thought Path Search via Logits Preference Decoding for Code Generation
ab: Code generation requires executable reasoning, making test-time chain-of-thought (CoT) search an attractive strategy for improving solution quality. However, existing CoT scaling methods often face a tension between underthinking, where shallow reasoning misses important algorithmic cases, and overthinking, where verbose or redundant reasoning consumes substantial tokens without improving correctness. We propose LogitsCoder, a lightweight framework that revisits CoT search from the perspective of logits-level control. LogitsCoder improves efficient reasoning search through two complementary mechanisms: Logits Preference Decoding adaptively calibrates local token expansion using public-test feedback, while Logits Rank Based Path Selection explores and selects compact high-confidence reasoning trajectories based on logit-level stability. Together with Thoughts Aggregation, LogitsCoder refines reasoning paths without relying on costly MCTS-style tree expansion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LogitsCoder produces more efficient and higher-quality reasoning chains, leading to superior code generation performance compared to baseline methods.

t: Towards Generalizable Visually Grounded Exploration of Household Devices
ab: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in static visual recognition and high-level semantic reasoning. However, current embodied exploration paradigms still heavily rely on imitation learning from human-annotated trajectories, which severely limits agents’ generalization ability. The key bottleneck of realizing general autonomous embodied agents lies in Generalizable Visually Grounded Exploration—the ability to operate novel devices without manuals or specific training by actively grounding abstract world knowledge into fine-grained visual affordances. Yet, existing benchmarks fail to evaluate this capability: they generally rely on explicit documents and annotated trajectories, neglecting the dynamic Hypothesis-Interaction-Refinement process essential for functional device operation. To bridge this gap, we introduce VGEBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate the generalizable visually grounded exploration capabilities of VLMs. Unlike static datasets, we construct a Logic-Driven State Machine framework. This framework simulates multi-turn interaction loops, compelling agents to achieve goals by active visual perception and feedback-driven correction. Experimental results demonstrate that existing VLMs face significant challenges in translating semantic knowledge into physical execution and maintaining long-horizon state tracking.

t: HybridProver: Augmenting Theorem Proving with LLM-Driven Proof Synthesis and Refinement
ab: Formal methods play a crucial role in ensuring the reliability of critical systems through rigorous mathematical verification. However, their adoption remains limited due to the labor-intensive nature of manual proof construction. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have opened new opportunities for automated theorem proving. Two main paradigms have emerged: stepwise tactic-based generation and whole-proof synthesis. While both approaches have complementary strengths, existing work largely treats them in isolation. In this work, we propose HybridProver, a unified framework that integrates whole-proof synthesis and tactic-based generation through proof sketches as an intermediate representation. This design enables the reuse of partially correct proof structures while effectively combining high-level planning with fine-grained reasoning. We implement HybridProver in Isabelle/HOL and post-train two 7B-scale LLMs on our optimized Isabelle datasets. Experiments on the miniF2F Isabelle benchmark achieved a 73.8% success rate and improved upon the previous state of the art (61.9%), demonstrating that lightweight models, when combined with our approach, can effectively generate Isabelle/HOL proofs without relying on very large LLMs. Ablation studies further analyze the impact of dataset quality, training configurations, and sampling strategies on proof generation. All code and datasets are released.

t: HyperPathsRAG: Multi-Target Path Approximation over Hypergraph Knowledge Graphs for Multi-Hop QA
a: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
ab: Multi-hop question answering needs evidence that is scattered across many sentences and ordered along a reasoning chain. Existing RAG systems struggle with this setting because flat chunk retrieval can miss bridge facts, binary graph structures lose n-ary information, and unordered top-K contexts leave evidence composition to the answer model. We introduce HyperPathsRAG, a hypergraph-based RAG framework that aligns query decomposition with the corpus index. It decomposes questions into n-ary sub-questions aligned with hypergraph facts, jointly matches all sub-questions to retrieve reasoning paths, scores paths by chain completeness, and presents the retrieved evidence in reasoning order. We evaluate in the candidate-passage setting on the 1k-question hard subsets of HotpotQA, 2Wiki, and MuSiQue, with three answering LLMs. HyperPathsRAG attains the best average Exact Match on every backbone (up to 42.2 EM / 56.2 F1 with Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct), and the best average F1 on two of three backbones; ablations attribute the bulk of the gain to the hypergraph index and the multi-target retriever. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HyperPathsRAG-AE05/.

t: GRAIN: Bridging Name and Narrative Shifts in Real-World Graph Reasoning through Invariance-Rewarded Agentic RL
a: Harbin Institute of Technology and Peng Cheng Laboratory
Beijing Baichuan Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd.
Beijing Baichuan Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd.
ab: Despite their potential in standardized graph tasks, Large Language Models (LLMs) remain brittle to real-world shifts in node identifiers and task formulation. While deterministic graph tools are invariant to such shifts, extracting topological structures from noisy text is highly fragile for LLMs, which often overfit to surface patterns. Moreover, mitigating these parsing failures via multi-agent systems incurs prohibitive latency. To address this, we propose GRAIN, a single-agent framework optimized via reinforcement learning. GRAIN models reasoning as a semantic parsing and tool-execution pipeline, guided by a Structure Invariance Reward. By validating extracted intermediate graphs against ground-truth topologies, this reward forces the LLM to learn robust text-to-structure mappings rather than memorizing linguistic artifacts. We also introduce GRIT, a benchmark evaluating sensitivity to such linguistic shifts. GRAIN outperforms multi-agent baselines by 16.45% in accuracy with approximately 24% lower latency. Furthermore, it demonstrates superior structural generalization, halving the out-of-distribution (OOD) gap of SFT models (from 15.77% to 7.80%) and maintaining robustness on large-scale graphs beyond the training distribution.

t: Counterfactual Selective Imitation for Long-Horizon Agents
ab: Long-horizon agents with structured actions execute tasks through sequences of dependent decisions, so a local decision mistake can change later observations and cause the task to fail. Stronger expert models offer a natural source of supervision, yet direct imitation or behavior cloning treats many differences between expert and base actions as equally useful targets. In this paper, we propose counterfactual selective imitation (CSI), a method that uses same-state counterfactual comparison to identify positive return differences. CSI assigns expert targets only when counterfactual rollouts show a high positive return difference, and routine states receive base-policy targets. The learned update is restricted to structured action spans, leaves the base model frozen, and does not require expert queries or replay at deployment. Experiments on AppWorld, ToolSandbox, and WebShop show that CSI raises average task success from 33.3% to 49.7% over the Qwen3-8B base and reduces average invalid/tool error from 9.3% to 4.9%. Compared with the strongest same-deployment adaptation baseline, CSI improves average task success by 1.3 points with only 5% additional deployed-inference latency.

t: Ada-SQL: Efficient and Adaptive Reasoning for Text-to-SQL
ab: Reasoning efficiency in Text-to-SQL is an important yet underexplored problem. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning models simplify traditional Text-to-SQL workflows and significantly improve the ability to handle complex queries. However, existing methods typically generate long reasoning processes for all queries. This leads to high token consumption and inference latency, increasing system cost and limiting practical deployment. To address this issue, we propose Ada-SQL, an adaptive reasoning model for Text-to-SQL that jointly optimizes reasoning mode selection and token budget control via a two-stage reinforcement learning framework coupled with a token budget model. This enables the model to adaptively decide whether to reason and how much reasoning budget to allocate based on query difficulty. Experimental results show that Ada-SQL reduces output token consumption by more than 65% while maintaining competitive execution accuracy, achieving a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off. Code and models will be released at https://github.com/sxhText2SQL/Ada-SQL.

t: Beyond Gradient Egalitarianism: Dual-Adaptive C-AUM Framework for Few-Shot Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
ab: While large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong text classification capabilities, adapting them to specialized, few-shot industrial domains remains challenging. Vanilla supervised fine-tuning (SFT) applies uniform weighting to training samples and may overfit easy instances while insufficiently optimizing ambiguous boundary samples. Static regularization may further limit adaptation by applying the same constraint throughout training. To address these limitations, we propose cumulative area under the margin (C-AUM), a fine-tuning framework tailored to autoregressive LLM classification. C-AUM tracks the cumulative margin of the final decision token as an instance-level difficulty signal and uses it to coordinate AUM-aware instance weighting with difficulty-aware dynamic LoRA regularization. We also construct and release an expert-verified few-shot text classification benchmark for the steel industry, comprising 1,070 samples across seven fine-grained categories. Evaluations across six representative LLMs show that C-AUM achieves comparable or improved performance over vanilla SFT, with a maximum macro F1 gain of 1.99 percentage points. Our dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/pengdada98/C-AUM.

t: Interpretable Oracle Bone Script Decipherment via Progressive Glyph Analysis with LVLMs
ab: Deciphering scanned Oracle Bone Script (OBS) images into corresponding modern Chinese characters is a crucial step in AI-assisted OBS decipherment. As a highly pictographic writing system, OBS often embeds semantic information in glyph forms, making its decipherment depend on more than visual similarity alone. However, how to effectively exploit such glyph-meaning cues and how to make the decipherment process interpretable remain challenging. To this end, we propose an LVLM-based framework that bridges glyphs and meanings through structured glyph analysis. Specifically, we introduce a progressive training strategy that guides the model from radical analysis to pictographic analysis and finally to mutual analysis, enabling it to capture semantic information embedded in OBS glyphs. The generated textual analyses serve as both interpretable reasoning traces and explicit evidence for retrieving corresponding modern Chinese characters from a dictionary. We also construct the Pictographic Decipherment OBS Dataset (PD-OBS), which provides detailed radical and pictographic analyses to support glyph-analysis learning and dictionary-based retrieval. Experiments on OBS benchmarks demonstrate the strong zero-shot capability of our method, especially its substantially improved Top-10 accuracy on unseen OBS, highlighting its ability to provide reliable and interpretable candidate references for AI-assisted archaeological and historical studies. The code and dataset will be released at https://github.com/PKXX1943/PD-OBS.

t: NUM2EVENT: Structured Event Inference from Numerical Time-Series
a: The University of Nottingham Ningbo China
ab: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong multimodal reasoning abilities, yet their understanding of purely numerical time-series remains limited. Existing approaches mainly focus on forecasting or trend description, providing little insight into the underlying events that have occurred or are unfolding within observed numerical dynamics. We study number-to-event reasoning and decoding, a task that infers interpretable and structured event hypotheses directly from numerical time-series when explicit event information is unavailable at inference time. The task focuses on aligned and plausible event semantics that help explain observed numerical dynamics. To address data scarcity and semantic alignment challenges, we propose a reasoning-aware framework that combines an agent-guided event extractor, a Hawkes-process-based synthetic data generator, and a multi-stage fine-tuning pipeline integrating a time-series encoder with a structured event decoder. The model generates intermediate reasoning steps and outputs constrained event representations. Experiments across multiple real-world domains show that our approach consistently outperforms strong LLM baselines in event-level precision and recall, demonstrating its effectiveness in bridging numerical reasoning and semantic event understanding. The code is available at https://github.com/feng1201/NUM2EVENT_IDEA

t: CQA-Eval: Designing Reliable Evaluations of Multi-paragraph Clinical QA under Resource Constraints
a: University of Washington and Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
ab: Evaluating multi-paragraph clinical question answering (QA) systems is resource-intensive and challenging: accurate judgments require medical expertise and achieving consistent human judgments over multi-paragraph text is difficult. We introduce CQA-Eval, an evaluation framework and set of evaluation recommendations for limited-resource and high-expertise settings. Based on physician annotations of 300 real patient questions answered by physicians and LLMs, we compare coarse answer-level versus fine-grained sentence-level evaluation over the dimensions of correctness, relevance, and risk disclosure. We find that inter-annotator agreement (IAA) varies by dimension: fine-grained annotation improves agreement on correctness, coarse improves agreement on relevance, and judgments on communicates-risks remain inconsistent. Additionally, annotating only a small subset of sentences can provide reliability comparable to coarse annotations, reducing cost and effort. Data and code available at https://github.com/federicabologna/cqa-eval under a CC-BY license.

t: APEX-Searcher: Hierarchical Credit Assignment with Subgoaling for Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
a: Institute of automation, Chinese academy of science
Institute of automation, Chinese academy of science, Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
ab: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) connects large language models (LLMs) to external knowledge, but single-round retrieval is often insufficient for complex multi-hop questions. To improve search on complex tasks, most existing works combine multi-round retrieval with reasoning through end-to-end training. While these approaches improve problem-solving performance, they still face challenges in task reasoning and model training. First, due to the lack of an explicit subgoaling mechanism, most existing RAG methods may produce ambiguous retrieval execution paths, leading to the degradation of model performance. Second, a few existing RAG methods have started to incorporate planning and execution into the model training process. However, they typically rely on a single final reward, causing hierarchical credit entanglement between planning and execution and preventing the model from clearly separating plan errors from retrieval errors. To address these limitations, we propose APEX-Searcher, a coordinated planner–executor framework that optimizes a recursive planner with RL to accommodate multiple valid, dependency-aware decompositions while training the executor with SFT under clearer subtask-level supervision. Extensive experiments show consistent gains in both multi-hop RAG and task planning across benchmarks.

t: When AI-Text Detectors Become Evidence: Rethinking Detection for Human Decisions
ab: AI-generated-text detectors are evaluated as classifiers, yet consequential deployments use detector outputs as evidence that people inspect, trust, contest, or use to escalate decisions. We call this mismatch the classification–evidence gap. The gap makes scalar detector scores a weak deployment interface: they hide the basis of a judgment, invite overtrust, and can turn false positives into accusations. We argue that AI-text detection should be evaluated as evidence-grounded decision support rather than as authorship proof. We introduce AGENT-XTrust, a guideline-expert detector that returns direct MetaAgent labels without target-domain scalar-cutoff calibration and converts each document-level judgment into inspectable evidence records containing local labels, rationales, confidence estimates, and linked spans. Across three domains and four generators, AGENT-XTrust preserves strong binary accuracy while producing inspectable, contestable evidence. In a controlled fixed-stimulus user study, participants assigned to the full AGENT-XTrust system-and-interface package achieved 19.8 and 11.3 points higher decision accuracy than those assigned to the score-only and score-plus-explanation packages, respectively; overtrust on each condition’s detector-wrong cases was 17.8 and 18.3 points lower. These results suggest a broader evaluation target for AI-text detection: not only whether a detector is correct, but whether complete detector-and-evidence packages support reliable human decisions under uncertainty.

t: Personalized Privacy Control in LLMs via Attention Head Intervention
ab: The rise of agentic AI enables LLMs to access diverse user data, raising critical privacy concerns. Prior work on contextual privacy studies whether LLMs regulate information disclosure according to context-dependent norms. However, acceptable disclosure boundaries may vary across users even within the same context. To address this limitation, we introduce personalized privacy, which incorporates user-specific disclosure preferences into privacy control. We further present P3Bench (Personalized Privacy Preservation Benchmark), a novel benchmark extending contextual privacy policies with personalized disclosure policies. Experiments show that prompt-based policies fail to reliably enforce personalized privacy policies, with Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma3-4B showing average policy ignorance ratios of 51.25% and 74.28%, respectively. Finally, to address this problem, we propose Repair, a robust inference-time attention head intervention method that adjusts disclosure behavior toward policy-consistent responses. Our method significantly improves adherence to user-specific privacy preferences by reducing cases where the model fails to follow the given policy.

t: SALUTE: Benchmarking and Adapting LLMs for the Defense Domain
ab: Defense is a knowledge-intensive domain that requires precise understanding of specialized terminology, doctrinal concepts, operational procedures, and evolving military events. Although recent work has explored language technologies for military applications, existing efforts remain fragmented: they are often task-specific, rely on limited adaptation pipelines, or lack comprehensive defense-domain evaluation. In this paper, we present **SALUTE**, an end-to-end framework for benchmarking and adapting LLMs for the defense domain. SALUTE integrates Salute-Corpus, a curated corpus from open-access U.S. military doctrine and government documents; Salute-Conv, a grounded instruction dataset from doctrinal sources and decade-long defense news; Salute-Pref, a defense-aware preference dataset; and Salute-Bench, a rigorously filtered benchmark for evaluating defense-domain understanding and reasoning over doctrine and defense news. Based on these resources, we train Salute-LLM through multi-stage post-training with continual pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and preference alignment. Extensive experiments show that Salute-LLM achieves strong defense-domain performance while retaining competitive general capabilities, demonstrating the effectiveness of SALUTE as an end-to-end framework for defense-domain LLM adaptation.

t: ICL4Decomp: Towards Re-executable Reverse Engineering
ab: Binary decompilation, which aims to recover source code from compiled binaries, can be viewed as a low-resource and high-constraint form of neural machine translation. However, existing decompilation techniques often fail to produce source code that can be successfully recompiled and re-executed, particularly for optimized binaries. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled neural approaches to decompilation, but the generated code is typically only semantically plausible rather than truly executable, limiting their practical reliability. These shortcomings arise from compiler optimizations and the loss of semantic cues in compiled code, which LLMs struggle to recover without contextual guidance. To address this challenge, we propose ICL4Decomp, a hybrid decompilation framework that leverages in-context learning (ICL) to guide LLMs toward generating re-executable source code. Notably, our approach is model-agnostic and requires no fine-tuning, enabling plug-and-play use with off-the-shelf LLMs. We evaluate ICL4Decomp across multiple datasets, optimization levels, and compilers, demonstrating around 40% improvement in re-executability over state-of-the-art decompilation methods while maintaining robustness.

t: Agentic Open-Domain Tabular Question Answering with Self-Supervised Multi-Table Retriever
a: the university of new south wales
ab: Open-domain tabular question answering (TQA) aims to answer natural language queries over a data lake that contains a large corpus of heterogeneous tables. Unlike closed-domain TQA, this task operates without pre-provided tables, making it particularly challenging. Existing methods usually first retrieve relevant tables and then answer the question based on the retrieved tables. However, it faces challenges in effectively and efficiently preparing tables from the low-quality, heterogeneous data lake and in operationalizing table information. To address these limitations, we present ArrTab (Agentic retrieval and reasoning on Tables) for open-domain TQA. ArrTab leverages MuRe, a self-supervised Multi-table Retriever trained on questions synthesized by translating table-derived SQL queries into natural language via large language models. Based on MuRe, ArrTab proposes a multi-agent system for open-domain TQA that consists of the Table Retriever Agent, the Table Integration Agent, the Information Extraction Agent and the Answer Agent. Furthermore, to enhance accuracy, a lazy execution strategy is adopted where operations are described in natural language but executed only during the information extraction stage, allowing for globally consistent reasoning. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of ArrTab.

t: Are Fine-Tuned LLM Membership Signals Real? Separating Memorization from Likelihood Shortcuts
a: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
ab: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) are increasingly used to audit whether protected examples were included in language model fine-tuning. Yet for fine-tuned LLMs, high attack AUC alone is not reliable evidence of data use: a score may separate members from non-members due to exposure, but also due to length, base model difficulty, typicality, or domain alignment. We propose DeMIA, a diagnostic membership inference framework that learns separate channels for membership scoring and difficulty modeling using likelihood features from the base and target models. DeMIA combines membership prediction with matched-pair ranking, base-difficulty anchoring, and adversarial length control, encouraging the final score to preserve membership-relevant evidence while reducing direct shortcut reliance. Across GPT-Neo-125M, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and Llama-3.1-8B on Wiki10k, AGNews10k, and XSum10k, DeMIA outperforms scalar likelihood, reference-calibrated, neighborhood, calibrated Min-K, and DF-style baselines while maintaining strong low-FPR recall. The signal remains strong on matched hard subsets, while blind controls using length, base loss, or other features from the base model remain near chance. These results show that fine-tuned LLM membership signals can persist under the tested nuisance controls and should be evaluated with reliability diagnostics rather than raw AUC alone.

t: DMDIntel: Interpreting Large Language Models via Dynamic Mode Decomposition
ab: In this work, we introduce DMDIntel which uses *dynamic mode decomposition* (DMD) to make the predictions made by LLMs in a classification task interpretable. It develops an input attribution pipeline, that first decomposes the hidden states of an LLM into prominent patterns, also known as *modes*, and then associates ranks to the input tokens based on the projection values on those modes. Rigorous experiments across three datasets and three model families consistently show that the ranked attribution of input tokens obtained using DMDIntel by far outperforms state-of-the-art techniques such as principal component analysis, integrated gradients and SHAP.

t: NGDBench: Towards Neural Graph Data Management
a: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
ab: Data critical to real-world decision-making is increasingly found within organizations. Such data is heterogeneous, constantly evolving, and only imperfectly captured. However, current data management systems remain largely passive, retrieving what is explicitly stored while offering limited support for uncovering implicit structure or reasoning under noise, incompleteness, and continuous updates. We argue that next-generation data management requires neural capabilities, which can uncover complex latent relationships, distinguish reliable signals from noise, and remain consistent as the underlying data state evolves. To support this direction, we introduce NGDBench, a benchmark across five domains that unifies structured and unstructured sources. NGDBench adopts a graph view because graphs provide a flexible abstraction for modeling complex systems, capturing latent relationships, and subsuming structured formats such as relational tables. Each instance pairs a clean latent graph with a realistically perturbed observed graph. NGDBench supports full Cypher queries and dynamic data management operations. Evaluations of state-of-the-art Text-to-Cypher by LLMs and GraphRAG pipelines reveal that current methods remain sensitive to noise and struggle with dynamic state tracking, highlighting the need for resilient, inference-capable data management. Our code is available at https://github.com/HKUST-KnowComp/NGDBench.

t: GlobeAudio: A Multilingual Multicultural Benchmark for Naturalistic Evaluation of Large Audio-Language Models
a: Singapore University of Technology and Design
Singapore University of Technology and Design
ab: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) integrate audio perception and language understanding within a unified framework, enabling a wide range of real-world applications. Despite recent advances, evaluation for LALMs remains heavily underspecified relative to real-world requirements: most lack true linguistic and cultural authenticity, while others fail to capture acoustic realism. To bridge this gap, we propose GlobeAudio, a multilingual and multicultural benchmark designed to evaluate naturalistic audio understanding. GlobeAudio consists of 5,637 multiple-choice questions across six typologically diverse languages, expertly crafted by native speakers grounded on naturally occurring audio. In order to do well, models must possess higher-level auditory reasoning skills and culturally grounded interpretation. We systematically evaluate representative closed-source and open-source LALMs, as well as cascaded ASR–LLM pipelines. Our experiments reveal substantial performance gaps under natural acoustic conditions, particularly for open-source models and low-resource languages. These findings highlight critical limitations of current LALMs and underscore the importance of naturalistic audio evaluation for future audio-language systems. GlobeAudio can be found at https://huggingface.co/datasets/iNLP-Lab/GlobeAudio.

t: Asuka-Bench: Benchmarking Code Agents on Underspecified User Intent and Multi-Round Refinement
a: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
University of Science and Technology of China
ab: Existing code-generation benchmarks score a single mapping from a complete prompt to a one-shot output. However, real web development is different. Users seldom write a full spec at the start; many requirements only become clear once they look at an intermediate result and react to it. We present Asuka-Bench, a benchmark that pairs underspecified user intent with multi-round refinement, grounded in browser-rendered behavior. Each task is resolved through a closed loop: a Code Agent generates a web project, a UI Agent executes test cases on the deployed site, and a User LLM turns evaluation outcomes into natural-language feedback for the next round. The benchmark comprises 50 web tasks with 784 evaluation criteria and 2402 expected outcomes. We benchmark 8 LLMs across 2 agent frameworks. The results separate models clearly: weighted Task Pass Rate varies by 38 percentage points and models also differ substantially in their ability to repair from feedback. Asuka-Bench is also far from saturated: even the strongest model completes only 52% of projects after three rounds.

t: All Claims Are Equal, but Some Claims Are More Equal Than Others: Importance-Sensitive Factuality Evaluation of LLM Generations
ab: Existing methods for evaluating the factuality of large language model (LLM) responses treat all claims as equally important. This results in misleading evaluations when vital information is missing or incorrect as it receives the same weight as peripheral details, raising the question: how can we reliably detect such differences when there are errors in key information? Current approaches that measure factuality tend to be insensitive to omitted or false key information. To investigate this lack of sensitivity, we construct VITALERRORS, a benchmark of 6,733 queries with minimally altered LLM responses designed to omit or falsify key information. Using this dataset, we demonstrate the insensitivities of existing evaluation metrics to key information errors. To address this gap, we introduce VITAL, a set of metrics that provide greater sensitivity in measuring the factuality of responses by incorporating the relevance and importance of claims with respect to the query. Our analysis demonstrates that VITAL metrics more reliably detect errors in key information than previous methods. Our dataset, metrics, and analysis provide a foundation for more accurate and robust assessment of LLM factuality.

t: “Not in My Backyard”: LLMs Uncover Online and Offline Social Biases Against Homelessness
a: United Nations University Institute in Macau
ab: Homelessness is a persistent social challenge, impacting millions worldwide. Over 876,000 people experiencing homelessness (PEH) were recorded in the U.S. in 2025. Social bias is a significant barrier to alleviating homelessness, shaping public perception and influencing policymaking. Because online textual media and offline city council discourse both reflect and influence public opinion, they provide valuable signals for identifying and tracking social biases against PEH. We release the first multi-domain PEH bias corpus with a 16-category multi-label taxonomy: a 1,698-item stratified gold-standard set annotated by partner-trained raters, plus 48,389 GPT-4.1-labeled texts, drawn from Reddit, X (formerly Twitter), news, and council meeting transcripts across ten U.S. cities (2015-2025). We benchmark six prompted LLMs on the gold-standard set and complement F1 with prevalence-gap audits. Moderate F1 coexists with large miscalibration: every model over-tags "not in my backyard" (NIMBY) (+11.5 pp) and under-detects factual claims (-30.5 pp). Error analysis on consensus false positives reveals that models treat housing vocabulary and question form as opposition proxies, producing NIMBY false positives on pro-service text. The corpus and audit protocol support municipal PEH stigma monitoring without treating teacher labels as ground truth.

t: TIGRIS: Integrating Policy Knowledge Graphs and Theory of Change for Institutionally Grounded Policy Impact Simulation
ab: Anticipating the social impacts of a policy prior to implementation requires institutional consistency: multi-agent reasoning must remain aligned with the rules specified in policy documents. However, existing LLM-based multi-agent simulations struggle to maintain such fine-grained institutional rules when policy documents are provided only as prompt context. In this paper, we propose TIGRIS, a Theory-guided framework for Institutionally Grounded policy Impact Simulation. TIGRIS (1) constructs a structured policy knowledge graph from natural-language policy documents, using the Institutional Analysis and Development framework to define institutional positions and Institutional Grammar 2.0 to encode behavioral rules; and (2) instantiates actor nodes as persona agents while anchoring them to a Theory of Change framework to map the causal pathways of policy impacts. Evaluated across four AI talent development policies and three LLMs, TIGRIS achieves the lowest macro-average MAPE, indicating that theory-guided institutional grounding supports domain-aligned reasoning for policy impact analysis.

t: ATC-Bench: A Simulation-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Generated Air Traffic Control Instructions
ab: Air traffic control (ATC) requires structured, safety-critical decision making whose effects unfold through aircraft trajectories, so text-level correctness alone is insufficient for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in this domain. We introduce ATC-Bench, a simulation-grounded benchmark for ATC instruction generation with Chinese-facing scenario descriptions and controller-style instruction fields. Given a structured Chinese traffic situation, a model generates a JSON control plan that is translated into BlueSky commands and evaluated through closed-loop simulation against separation, no-fly-zone (NFZ) avoidance, and route-recovery constraints. The benchmark spans four task families that form a controlled complexity gradient: single-aircraft NFZ avoidance, pairwise conflict resolution, joint conflict-airspace constraints, and multi-aircraft conflict graphs. Experiments with 11 representative LLM endpoints show that while most models produce format-valid instructions, task success varies widely across models and task families: the highest-scoring endpoint under our fixed protocol achieves 63.5% macro-average task success rate (TSR), while the two lowest endpoints fall below 25%, with the largest gaps appearing under joint constraints and multi-aircraft coordination. These results expose a persistent execution gap between static validity and simulation-passing behavior, motivating simulation-in-the-loop evaluation for LLM-based decision making in safety-critical aviation settings.

t: A Tree-based RAG Framework for Evidence-Intensive QA via Adaptive Planning and Topology-Aware Evidence Gathering
ab: Recent structured RAG methods leverage tree- or graph-based reasoning structures to improve multi-hop QA. However, they face key limitations in evidence-intensive QA, where answering a question requires synthesizing information scattered across dozens or even hundreds of documents: structural rigidity, which limits adaptive reasoning expansion, and topology-ignorant evidence gathering, which prevents effective integration of evidence across different reasoning nodes. To address these issues, we propose APT-RAG, an Adaptive Planning and Topology-aware evidence gathering RAG framework. Adaptive planning dynamically expands the reasoning structure based on question dependencies and evidence requirements, while topology-aware evidence gathering improves evidence coverage through sibling evidence reuse, direct retrieval, and evidence aggregation from child nodes. We further introduce evidence-guided batched answer generation to reduce significant generation overhead in evidence-intensive QA. In the experiments on evidence-intensive QA benchmarks, APT-RAG outperforms existing structured RAG methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/hyudsl/APT-RAG.

t: OpenSkillEval: Automatically Auditing the Open Skill Ecosystem for LLM Agents
ab: Skills are increasingly used to improve LLM agents on real-world tasks, yet it remains unclear how agents use skills, how skill quality should be evaluated, and how users should choose skills under cost-performance trade-offs. We present OpenSkillEval, an automatic framework for evaluating both skill-augmented agents and skills. OpenSkillEval dynamically constructs test cases from evolving real-world artifacts across five applications: presentation generation, front-end web design, poster generation, data visualization, and report generation. It also curates community skills for controlled comparison under unified settings. Using over 600 generated tasks and 30 open-source skills, we evaluate state-of-the-art models and agent frameworks. Results show that skill availability does not guarantee effective use, skill benefits depend strongly on the model and framework, and many popular skills fail to consistently outperform skill-free agents. These findings highlight the need for dynamic, task-grounded evaluation and offer practical guidance for skill design, selection, and deployment.

t: GraDuLa: Graph-based Dual-branch Language-agnostic Modeling for Misinformation Detection with Cross-lingual Evidences
a: Fujitsu Research and Development Center Co. Ltm.
Fujitsu Research and Development Center Co. Ltm.
ab: Misinformation detection has predominantly been studied in monolingual or language-aligned settings, where claims and evidences are assumed to be written in the same language. However, this assumption does not reflect real-world information ecosystems, in which misinformation frequently spans multiple languages and verification requires cross-lingual reasoning over heterogeneous evidence sources. As a result, cross-lingual claim-evidence reasoning remains largely unexplored and has not been systematically studied, and existing methods are not explicitly designed to support such scenarios. To address this gap, we introduce a novel setting for multilingual misinformation detection with cross-lingual evidences and propose GraDuLa, a graph-based dual-branch language-agnostic modeling for misinformation detection. GraDuLa projects evidential information into a language-agnostic subspace, disentangling semantic representations from language-specific associations through dual-branch graph modeling. For evaluation, we construct and release a benchmark GraDuLaEval and compare our approach against strong baseline methods. We further plan to release the dual-branch graph representations as an additional resource for future research.

t: FServe: FP8-Native W4A8KV4 Quantization and Attention Kernel Optimization for Efficient LLM Serving
ab: As large language models (LLMs) scale, inference throughput is increasingly bottlenecked by memory bandwidth. While prior 4-bit quantization schemes promise memory savings, their dequantization overhead often negates these gains. We present FServe, a hardware-software co-designed framework featuring an FP8-native W4A8KV4 scheme that combines channel pre-scaling and group-wise scale relaxation for linear layers with post-RoPE key smoothing that aligns channel-wise means and ranges for attention layers. To translate these memory savings into FP8-native throughput, FServe further extends FlashAttention-3 kernels for prefill with packed-FP16 softmax instruction reordering and multi-warp asynchronous TMA fetching, and introduces a dynamic Stream-KV tile scheduler for decode phase workload imbalance. Our evaluation on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B shows that FServe outperforms AWQ W4A16 and W4A8 baselines on accuracy despite additionally compressing the KV cache to INT4, achieves up to 1.41× TTFT speedup over BF16, and sustains effective decode bandwidth above the H100’s theoretical peak.

t: EviDx: Evidence-Aware Active Diagnosis with Scaffolded LLM Agents
a: Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory and Sensetime
ab: Clinical diagnosis is an active evidence-seeking process in which clinicians acquire evidence, update competing hypotheses, and decide when the available evidence is sufficient for diagnosis. Yet many medical diagnosis systems built around large language models (LLMs) still formulate diagnosis as static case-to-answer prediction, with limited support for evidence acquisition. Agentic LLMs offer a dynamic alternative through tool use and intermediate diagnostic trajectories, but existing systems often under-specify how patient evidence should be exposed, scaffolded, and controlled at runtime. We introduce EviDx, an evidence-aware active diagnosis framework that pairs patient-specific diagnostic environments with a clinical diagnostic scaffold and an observer-guided runtime harness. In EviDx, \mathcal{E}-Synthesis constructs interactive environments from raw clinical cases; the scaffold organizes role-specialized agents, evidence tools, and evolving evidence states; and the harness regulates diagnostic termination by tracking uncertainty and evidence coverage. A 3-level evaluation pyramid assesses execution robustness, reasoning dynamics, and diagnostic outcomes. Experiments show that EviDx improves diagnostic performance and process stability while revealing model-dependent capability boundaries.

t: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy
a: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
ab: Large language models can answer a medical question correctly and still abandon that answer when a user pushes back. We study this failure as medical sycophancy and ask when models are most likely to give in. Across five open-weight models, 500 MEDQUAD questions, and 1.2 million trials, we use a fully crossed design over four conversational factors: user role, user evidence, interaction structure, and grounding. Medical sycophancy is nearly three times more common when users challenge an answer the model has already given than when the false claim appears in the initial query. Models are also more susceptible to users presented as physicians or medical students. Most strikingly, fabricated evidence has opposite effects across interaction structures. It increases sycophancy in single-turn interactions but reduces it after the model has already answered. Grounding helps, but does not eliminate the behavior. Sycophancy varies more across medical questions than across models, making question selection an important part of benchmark design. Reasoning traces suggest that multi-turn failures are associated with models turning back toward their own prior answer, while fabricated evidence receives more scrutiny after an initial response. Together, the results show that medical sycophancy depends as much on how a model is challenged and evaluated as on which model is tested.

t: SAUL: Sharpness-Aware Augmented-Lagrangian Unlearning
a: Pohang University of Science and Technology
Pohang University of Science and Technology
ab: Machine unlearning in Large Language Models (LLMs) faces a critical trade-off between erasing target knowledge and preserving general utility. We propose SAUL (Sharpness-Aware Augmented-Lagrangian Unlearning), which formulates unlearning as a constrained minimization problem following the principle of “forget enough, but no more than necessary.” At its core, SAUL formulates forgetting as an explicit constraint with a prescribed satisfaction criterion, whereas prior unlearning methods typically specify the desired level of forgetting implicitly through optimization objectives. An augmented Lagrangian controller adaptively adjusts forget-side pressure according to constraint violation and can eventually deactivate the forget-side update as the prescribed criterion remains satisfied. Sharpness-aware updates on both retain and forget objectives, together with a dual-optimizer design that maintains role-separated states, further stabilize the resulting unlearning dynamics. We evaluate SAUL on the TOFU, WMDP, and MUSE benchmarks, demonstrating favorable forgetting–utility trade-offs over representative sharpness- and perturbation-based baselines under benchmark-specific forgetting criteria. Beyond the complete SAUL framework, we further show on TOFU and WMDP that applying the augmented-Lagrangian controller as a drop-in modifier to representative baselines improves their post-forgetting utility, demonstrating the practical value of explicit forgetting control.

t: Communicating Chess Strategies in Natural Language
ab: Chess engines have long achieved superhuman playing strength. However, the underlying strategy behind their move suggestions is difficult for human players, even skilled ones, to comprehend. Motivated by this, we propose the task of chess *strategy verbalization*, which is to describe chess strategies in natural language. We design (i) a pipeline for verbalizing strategies and (ii) an evaluation framework for objective evaluation of generated strategy descriptions. Our experiments show that natural language is a promising and interpretable medium for communicating strategic information to both human and LLM players. We glean additional interesting insights, including (a) the importance of evaluating strategies beyond the main line, (b) the limitations of pure concept-based descriptions, and (c) the limitations of relying on LLMs rather than humans for evaluation.

t: Visual Representation Regularization for Multimodal Hallucination Mitigation
ab: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in multimodal reasoning, yet they still suffer from hallucinations that undermine their reliability. Existing inference-time mitigation methods mainly focus on optimizing decoding strategies or analyzing internal attention mechanisms, while the role of visual representations remains underexplored. In this work, we reveal that visual representations exhibit information dispersion during layer-wise evolution, manifested as a progressive deviation from the initial visual subspace and increasing alignment with the textual subspace. Based on this insight, we propose Visual Representation Regularization (VRR), a training-free method that mitigates hallucinations by regularizing visual representations toward their initial states. Extensive experiments demonstrate that VRR consistently reduces hallucinations and is compatible with existing mitigation methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/Jiarker/VRR.

t: Neuron-Guided Fine-Tuning: Unlocking Efficient Alignment Mechanisms for Large Language Models
ab: Existing Supervised Fine-Tuning paradigms, particularly Full Parameter Fine-Tuning are often plagued by parameter redundancy, inconsistent data quality, and catastrophic forgetting, which current methods typically address in isolation and lack a unified optimization signal to bridge data selection, parameter updates, and knowledge preservation. To address this, we propose Neuron-Guided Fine-Tuning (NGFT), a holistic framework that leverages neuron activation patterns as a universal proxy to unify the fine-tuning lifecycle. NGFT operates via three synergistic mechanisms: (1) Adaptive Task-Specific Neuron Selection, which identifies essential neurons in a single forward pass to concentrate updates and reduce redundancy; (2) Activation-Based Data Selection, which prioritizes information-dense samples that maximize contribution to key neurons; and (3) Neuron Activation Alignment, a novel loss function that anchors activations to pre-trained states, deepening representation learning and preserving general knowledge. Experimental results across three models across both domain-specific and general benchmarks demonstrate that NGFT significantly outperforms existing mainstream fine-tuning methods in both efficiency and performance, while effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting.

t: Plan the Semantics, Then Render the Signal: A Hybrid State-Space Model for Incomplete Multimodal Learning
a: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
ab: Incomplete multimodal learning seeks robust perception when modalities are absent at training or test time, using available streams to recover the missing ones. Most methods cast this as direct regression in a fixed continuous latent, which (i) collapses many valid solutions into an averaged reconstruction when observations underdetermine the target, and (ii) suffers semantic drift when cross-modal relationships shift with context. We argue that completion should first resolve what is missing and only then render how it appears. We realize this as Semantic-first Completion, instantiated by a Hybrid State-Space Model (HySSM) that decouples semantic intent from signal realization. A frozen omni-modal LLM plans over observation-only evidence, generating an evidence-grounded Markovian trajectory of discrete semantic states that act as a compact information bottleneck for stable cross-modal reasoning. The plan is projected into a coordinate-wise control field that drift-guides a conditional diffusion model, synthesizing missing signals or feature streams as diverse and semantically consistent completions. Across MNIST, Hateful Memes, and CMU-MOSEI, HySSM surpasses recent generative baselines and, under agnostic masking shift, remains robust up to 90% missingness.

t: A Thousand Words or An Image: Studying the Influence of Persona Modality in Multimodal LLMs
ab: Language models have demonstrated remarkable advancements in embodying diverse personas, enhancing their effectiveness as conversational agents. Simultaneously, there have been significant strides in these models in processing and integrating visual information. However, despite images being a natural carrier of persona attributes (e.g. age, occupation, or location), it remains largely unexplored whether multimodal language models (MLLMs) can faithfully ground visual persona information. In this work, we introduce persona embodiment as a novel diagnostic for visual grounding in MLLMs. Unlike simple visual recognition, this task requires models to extract multiple persona attributes from an image, integrate them into a coherent representation, and apply them to downstream language tasks. To this end, we introduce a modality-parallel dataset of personas, containing 2,400 prompts each represented in four modalities. Across our experiments, we find that models frequently underuse visual information relative to text, and that this neglect persists even when richer visual information is clearly available, highlighting underlying limitations and paving the way for future research to bridge this gap.

t: Learning Structured Emotional Dynamics in Latent Space via Trajectory Modeling and Controlled Transitions
ab: Emotion understanding from text has been predominantly approached through discrete classification frameworks. However, complementary perspectives in psychology and neuroscience suggest that affective states may also exhibit continuous, context-dependent, and temporally structured properties. Building on this perspective, we investigate emotion representations as latent dynamical trajectories within transformer embedding spaces. Using GoEmotions and MELD across four transformer architectures, we analyze the geometric organization and temporal evolution of learned emotional states. We find that latent trajectories exhibit temporal persistence and structured transition dynamics, while the prediction error increases during emotion shifts, acting as a signal of expectation violation. We additionally introduce trajectory-level latent interventions enabling controllable emotional transitions through directional operations in representation space. Finally, manifold capacity analysis reveals partially aligned and variably separable emotional manifolds, suggesting shared geometric organization across affective representations.

t: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation for GUI Agents
a: University of Science and Technology Beijing
ab: Improving GUI agents typically relies on behavior cloning on expert trajectories. However, as the current policy deviates from the expert policy, it inevitably encounters policy-induced off-trajectory states during closed-loop execution, i.e., states that fall outside the expert trajectories. Since expert trajectories provide no demonstrations for these unseen states, such states receive no effective supervision, leaving the policy unable to select the correct action.
